items.name: narrator
items.text: The vision of Yahshayahu son of Amots, which he saw concerning Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim in the days of Uzziyahu, Yotham, Aḥaz, Ḥizqiyahu – sovereigns of Yahuḏah.
items.kk: The vision of yah-shah-yah-hoo son of Amots, which he saw concerning yah-hoo-dah and yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem in the days of Uzziyahu, Yotham, ah-khahz, Kizqiyahu, sovereigns of yah-hoo-dah.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Yahrushalayim, about 740 BCE. The words of Yahshayahu son of Amots span the reigns of four sovereigns of Yahuḏah — from the year Uzziyahu died, about 740, into the days of Ḥizqiyahu, to about 701.
items.kk: yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, about 740 B.C.E. The words of yah-shah-yah-hoo son of Amots span the reigns of four sovereigns of yah-hoo-dah, from the year Uzziyahu died, about 740, into the days of Kizqiyahu, to about 701.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: In the year that Sovereign Uzziyahu died, I saw (YAHUAH) HWHY sitting on a throne, high and lifted up and the train of His robe filled the Hĕḵal.
items.kk: In the year that Sovereign Uzziyahu died, I saw YAHUAH sitting on a throne, high and lifted up and the train of His robe filled the hay-kahl.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: Above it stood seraphim. Each one had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet and with two he flew.
items.kk: Above it stood seraphim. Each one had six wings, with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet and with two he flew.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And one cried to another and said,
items.kk: And one cried to another and said,

items.name: seraph
items.text: “Qadash (Set Apart), qadash (Set Apart), qadash (Set Apart) is (YAHUAH) HWHY of hosts; all the earth is filled with His esteem!”
items.kk: kah-dahsh, kah-dahsh, kah-dahsh is YAHUAH of hosts, all the earth is filled with His esteem!

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And the posts of the door were shaken by the voice of him who cried out and the house was filled with smoke.
items.kk: And the posts of the door were shaken by the voice of him who cried out and the house was filled with smoke.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And I said,
items.kk: And I said,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Woe to me, for I am undone! Because I am a man of unclean lips and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips – for my eyes have seen the Sovereign, (YAHUAH) HWHY of hosts.”
items.kk: Woe to me, for I am undone! Because I am a man of unclean lips and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips, for my eyes have seen the Sovereign, YAHUAH of hosts.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from the mizbe'ach.
items.kk: And one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from the miz-beh-ahk.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And he touched my mouth with it and said,
items.kk: And he touched my mouth with it and said,

items.name: seraph
items.text: “See, this has touched your lips; your crookedness is taken away and your sin is covered.”
items.kk: See, this has touched your lips, your crookedness is taken away and your sin is covered.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And I heard the voice of (YAHUAH) HWHY, saying,
items.kk: And I heard the voice of YAHUAH, saying,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Whom do I send and who would go for Us?”
items.kk: Whom do I send and who would go for Us?

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Here am I! Send me.”
items.kk: Here am I! Send me.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And He said,
items.kk: And He said,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Go and you shall say to this people, ‘Hearing, you hear, but do not understand; and seeing, you see, but do not know.’
items.kk: Go and you shall say to this people, Hearing, you hear, but do not understand, and seeing, you see, but do not know.

items.name: divine
items.text: “Make the heart of this people fat and their ears heavy and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and shall turn and be healed.”
items.kk: Make the heart of this people fat and their ears heavy and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and shall turn and be healed.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: Then I said,
items.kk: Then I said,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “(YAHUAH) HWHY, until when?”
items.kk: YAHUAH, until when?

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And He answered,
items.kk: And He answered,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Until the cities are laid waste and without inhabitant and the houses are without a man and the land is laid waste, a ruin,
items.kk: Until the cities are laid waste and without inhabitant and the houses are without a man and the land is laid waste, a ruin,

items.name: divine
items.text: and (YAHUAH) HWHY has removed men far away and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.
items.kk: and YAHUAH has removed men far away and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.

items.name: divine
items.text: “But still, there is a tenth part in it and it shall again be for a burning, like a terebinth tree and like an oak, whose stump remains when it is cut down. The qadash (Set Apart) seed is its stump!”
items.kk: But still, there is a tenth part in it and it shall again be for a burning, like a terebinth tree and like an oak, whose stump remains when it is cut down. The kah-dahsh seed is its stump!

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it came to be in the days of Aḥaz son of Yotham, son of Uzziyahu, sovereign of Yahuḏah, that Retsin sovereign of Aram and Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, sovereign of Yasharal, went up to Yahrushalayim to fight against it, but could not prevail against it.
items.kk: And it came to be in the days of ah-khahz son of Yotham, son of Uzziyahu, sovereign of yah-hoo-dah, that Retsin sovereign of Aram and Peqak son of Remalyahu, sovereign of yah-shar-al, went up to yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem to fight against it, but could not prevail against it.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it was reported to the house of Dawiḏ, saying,
items.kk: And it was reported to the house of dah-veed, saying,

items.name: those who brought word
items.text: “Aram has set up camp in Ephrayim.”
items.kk: Aram has set up camp in Ephrayim.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And his heart and the heart of his people were moved as the trees of the forest are moved with the ruach.
items.kk: And his heart and the heart of his people were moved as the trees of the forest are moved with the roo-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: About 735 BCE. Aram and the northern kingdom have marched against Yahrushalayim to force Yahuḏah into their war against Ashshur. The city is afraid.
items.kk: About 735 B.C.E. Aram and the northern kingdom have marched against yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem to force yah-hoo-dah into their war against ah-shoor. The city is afraid.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And (YAHUAH) HWHY said to Yahshayahu,
items.kk: And YAHUAH said to yah-shah-yah-hoo,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Go out now to meet Aḥaz, you and She’ar-Yashuḇ your son, at the end of the channel of the upper pool, on the highway of the Launderer’s Field,
items.kk: Go out now to meet ah-khahz, you and Shear-Yashub your son, at the end of the channel of the upper pool, on the highway of the Launderer's Field,

items.name: divine
items.text: and say to him, ‘Take heed and be calm; do not fear or be faint-hearted for these two stubs of smoking fire brands, for the fierce displeasure of Retsin and Aram and the son of Remalyahu.
items.kk: and say to him, Take heed and be calm, do not fear or be faint-hearted for these two stubs of smoking fire brands, for the fierce displeasure of Retsin and Aram and the son of Remalyahu.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And (YAHUAH) HWHY spoke again to Aḥaz, saying,
items.kk: And YAHUAH spoke again to ah-khahz, saying,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Ask a sign for yourself from (YAHUAH) HWHY your Aluahim; make deep the request or make it high.”
items.kk: Ask a sign for yourself from YAHUAH your al-oo-ah-heem, make deep the request or make it high.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Aḥaz said,
items.kk: But ah-khahz said,

items.name: ahaz
items.text: “I do not ask nor try (YAHUAH) HWHY!”
items.kk: I do not ask nor try YAHUAH!

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he said,
items.kk: And he said,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Hear now, O house of Dawiḏ! Is it not enough that you weary men, that you weary my Aluahim also?
items.kk: Hear now, O house of dah-veed! Is it not enough that you weary men, that you weary my al-oo-ah-heem also?

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Therefore (YAHUAH) HWHY Himself gives you a sign: Look, the maiden conceives and gives birth to a Son and shall call His Name Immanu’al.
items.kk: Therefore YAHUAH Himself gives you a sign, Look, the maiden conceives and gives birth to a Son and shall call His Name ee-mah-noo-ahl.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You read the board over twice. Not one word of it is yours to change.
items.kk: You read the board over twice. Not one word of it is yours to change.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You do not know. The words are kept; their hour will come.
items.kk: You do not know. The words are kept, their hour will come.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: Bind up the witness and seal the Torah among my taught ones.
items.kk: Bind up the witness and seal the toh-rah among my taught ones.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: For a Child shall be born unto us, a Son shall be given unto us and the rule is on His shoulder. And His Name is called Wonder, Counsellor, Strong Al, Father of Continuity, Prince of Shalom. Of the increase of His rule and shalom there is no end, upon the throne of Dawiḏ and over His reign, to establish it and sustain it with right-ruling and with righteousness from now on, even forever. The ardour of (YAHUAH) HWHY of hosts does this.
items.kk: For a Child shall be born unto us, a Son shall be given unto us and the rule is on His shoulder. And His Name is called Wonder, Counsellor, Strong Al, Father of Continuity, Prince of shah-lohm. Of the increase of His rule and shah-lohm there is no end, upon the throne of dah-veed and over His reign, to establish it and sustain it with right-ruling and with righteousness from now on, even forever. The ardour of YAHUAH of hosts does this.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The years go by — the reign of Aḥaz ends, and Ḥizqiyahu his son reigns. The words go on being given, and the taught ones go on keeping them.
items.kk: The years go by, the reign of ah-khahz ends, and Kizqiyahu his son reigns. The words go on being given, and the taught ones go on keeping them.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And a Rod shall come forth from the stump of Yahshai and a Sprout from his roots shall bear fruit. The Ruach of (YAHUAH) HWHY shall rest upon Him – the Ruach of wisdom and understanding, the Ruach of counsel and might, the Ruach of knowledge and of the fear of (YAHUAH) HWHY,
items.kk: And a Rod shall come forth from the stump of yah-shy and a Sprout from his roots shall bear fruit. The roo-ahk of YAHUAH shall rest upon Him, the roo-ahk of wisdom and understanding, the roo-ahk of counsel and might, the roo-ahk of knowledge and of the fear of YAHUAH,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened and the ears of the deaf be opened. Then the lame shall leap like a deer and the tongue of the dumb sing, because waters shall burst forth in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
items.kk: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened and the ears of the deaf be opened. Then the lame shall leap like a deer and the tongue of the dumb sing, because waters shall burst forth in the wilderness and streams in the desert.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: The voice of one crying in the wilderness,
items.kk: The voice of one crying in the wilderness,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Prepare the way of (YAHUAH) HWHY; make straight in the desert a highway for our Aluahim.
items.kk: Prepare the way of YAHUAH, make straight in the desert a highway for our al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: despised and rejected by men, a man of pains and knowing sickness. And as one from whom the face is hidden, being despised and we did not consider Him. Truly, He has borne our sicknesses and carried our pains. Yet we reckoned Him stricken, smitten by Aluahim and afflicted. But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our crookednesses. The chastisement for our shalom was upon Him and by His stripes we are healed.
items.kk: despised and rejected by men, a man of pains and knowing sickness. And as one from whom the face is hidden, being despised and we did not consider Him. Truly, He has borne our sicknesses and carried our pains. Yet we reckoned Him stricken, smitten by al-oo-ah-heem and afflicted. But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our crookednesses. The chastisement for our shah-lohm was upon Him and by His stripes we are healed.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: The Ruach of the Master (YAHUAH) HWHY is upon Me, because (YAHUAH) HWHY has anointed Me to bring the besorah to the meek. He has sent Me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim release to the captives and the opening of the prison to those who are bound, to proclaim the acceptable year of (YAHUAH) HWHY and the day of vengeance of our Aluahim, to comfort all who mourn,
items.kk: The roo-ahk of the Master YAHUAH is upon Me, because YAHUAH has anointed Me to bring the beh-soh-rah to the meek. He has sent Me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim release to the captives and the opening of the prison to those who are bound, to proclaim the acceptable year of YAHUAH and the day of vengeance of our al-oo-ah-heem, to comfort all who mourn,

items.name: narrator
items.text: Seven words, copied in your own hand. You tie the cord. Your children will keep it, and theirs after them.
items.kk: Seven words, copied in your own hand. You tie the cord. Your children will keep it, and theirs after them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You read them in the dawn light, from the sign at the upper pool to the one who was pierced.
items.kk: You read them in the dawn light, from the sign at the upper pool to the one who was pierced.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: And I shall wait on (YAHUAH) HWHY, who hides His face from the house of Ya‛aqoḇ. And I shall look for Him.
items.kk: And I shall wait on YAHUAH, who hides His face from the house of Yaaqob. And I shall look for Him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The fourteenth year of Ḥizqiyahu. c. 701 BCE
items.kk: The fourteenth year of Kizqiyahu. about 701 B.C.E.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it came to be in the fourteenth year of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu that Sanḥĕriḇ sovereign of Ashshur came up against all the walled cities of Yahuḏah and took them.
items.kk: And it came to be in the fourteenth year of Sovereign Kizqiyahu that Sankerib sovereign of ah-shoor came up against all the walled cities of yah-hoo-dah and took them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: About 701 BCE. Sanḥĕriḇ’s own annals, found at Ninewĕh, boast of taking forty-six walled cities of Yahuḏah and of shutting Ḥizqiyahu up in Yahrushalayim “like a bird in a cage” — but they do not claim the city. His palace walls show the siege of Laḵish.
items.kk: About 701 B.C.E. Sankeribs own annals, found at Nineweh, boast of taking forty-six walled cities of yah-hoo-dah and of shutting Kizqiyahu up in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem like a bird in a cage, but they do not claim the city. His palace walls show the siege of Lakish.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu saw that Sanḥĕriḇ had come and his face set to fight against Yahrushalayim,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu saw that Sankerib had come and his face set to fight against yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and he took counsel with his rulers and mighty men to stop the water from the springs which were outside the city. And they helped him.
items.kk: and he took counsel with his rulers and mighty men to stop the water from the springs which were outside the city. And they helped him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And many people were gathered and they stopped all the springs and the stream that ran through the land, saying,
items.kk: And many people were gathered and they stopped all the springs and the stream that ran through the land, saying,

items.name: people
items.text: “Why should the sovereigns of Ashshur come and find much water?”
items.kk: Why should the sovereigns of ah-shoor come and find much water?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu himself had stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Giḥon and directed them to the west side of the City of Dawiḏ. And Ḥizqiyahu prospered in all his work.
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu himself had stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gikon and directed them to the west side of the City of dah-veed. And Kizqiyahu prospered in all his work.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The channel he cut is there still: 533 metres through the rock beneath the City of Dawiḏ, from the spring of Giḥon to the pool of Shiloaḥ. An inscription found in it in 1880 tells how the two crews of hewers, cutting from either end, heard each other’s picks through the rock and met.
items.kk: The channel he cut is there still, 533 metres through the rock beneath the City of dah-veed, from the spring of Gikon to the pool of Shiloak. An inscription found in it in 1880 tells how the two crews of hewers, cutting from either end, heard each other's picks through the rock and met.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the sovereign of Ashshur sent the Raḇshaqĕh with a great army from Laḵish to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu at Yahrushalayim. And he stood by the channel of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer’s Field.
items.kk: And the sovereign of ah-shoor sent the Rabshaqeh with a great army from Lakish to Sovereign Kizqiyahu at yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem. And he stood by the channel of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And there came to him Alyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household and Sheḇnah the scribe and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder.
items.kk: And there came to him Alyaqim son of Kilqiyahu, who was over the household and Shebnah the scribe and Yoak son of Asaph, the recorder.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The Raḇshaqĕh then said to them,
items.kk: The Rabshaqeh then said to them,

items.name: rabshaqeh
items.text: “Please say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur, “What trust is this in which you trust?
items.kk: Please say to Kizqiyahu, Thus said the great sovereign, the sovereign of ah-shoor, What trust is this in which you trust?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the Raḇshaqĕh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of Yahuḏah and said,
items.kk: And the Rabshaqeh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of yah-hoo-dah and said,

items.name: rabshaqeh
items.text: “Hear the words of the great sovereign, the sovereign of Ashshur!
items.kk: Hear the words of the great sovereign, the sovereign of ah-shoor!

items.name: rabshaqeh
items.text: “Thus said the sovereign, ‘Do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive you, for he is unable to deliver you,
items.kk: Thus said the sovereign, Do not let Kizqiyahu deceive you, for he is unable to deliver you,

items.name: rabshaqeh
items.text: and do not let Ḥizqiyahu make you trust in (YAHUAH) HWHY, saying,
items.kk: and do not let Kizqiyahu make you trust in YAHUAH, saying,

items.name: rabshaqeh
items.text: “(YAHUAH) HWHY shall certainly deliver us, this city is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.”
items.kk: YAHUAH shall certainly deliver us, this city is not given into the hand of the sovereign of ah-shoor.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But they were silent and answered him not a word, for the command of the sovereign was,
items.kk: But they were silent and answered him not a word, for the command of the sovereign was,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “Do not answer him.”
items.kk: Do not answer him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Alyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, Sheḇnah the scribe and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Ḥizqiyahu with their garments torn and they reported to him the words of the Raḇshaqĕh.
items.kk: And Alyaqim son of Kilqiyahu, who was over the household, Shebnah the scribe and Yoak son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Kizqiyahu with their garments torn and they reported to him the words of the Rabshaqeh.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You hold your tongue on the wall with the others. Below, the army of Ashshur waits.
items.kk: You hold your tongue on the wall with the others. Below, the army of ah-shoor waits.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Thirty years ago, here at the upper pool, the naḇi gave a sign to Aḥaz. You still have the board you wrote it on.
items.kk: Thirty years ago, here at the upper pool, the nah-vee gave a sign to ah-khahz. You still have the board you wrote it on.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it came to be, when Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu heard it, that he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the House of (YAHUAH) HWHY,
items.kk: And it came to be, when Sovereign Kizqiyahu heard it, that he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the House of YAHUAH,

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu received the letter from the hand of the mal'akim and read it. And Ḥizqiyahu went up to the House of (YAHUAH) HWHY and spread it before (YAHUAH) HWHY.
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu received the letter from the hand of the mahl-ah-keem and read it. And Kizqiyahu went up to the House of YAHUAH and spread it before YAHUAH.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu prayed to (YAHUAH) HWHY,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu prayed to YAHUAH,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “O (YAHUAH) HWHY of hosts, Aluahim of Yasharal, the One who dwells between the keruḇim, You are Aluahim, You alone, of all the reigns of the earth. You have made the shamayim and earth.
items.kk: O YAHUAH of hosts, al-oo-ah-heem of yah-shar-al, the One who dwells between the kerubim, You are al-oo-ah-heem, You alone, of all the reigns of the earth. You have made the shah-mah-yeem and earth.

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “And now, O (YAHUAH) HWHY our Aluahim, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that You are (YAHUAH) HWHY, You alone.”
items.kk: And now, O YAHUAH our al-oo-ah-heem, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that You are YAHUAH, You alone.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then Yahshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying,
items.kk: Then yah-shah-yah-hoo son of Amots sent to Kizqiyahu, saying,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Thus said (YAHUAH) HWHY Aluahim of Yasharal, ‘Because you have prayed to Me against Sanḥĕriḇ sovereign of Ashshur,
items.kk: Thus said YAHUAH al-oo-ah-heem of yah-shar-al, Because you have prayed to Me against Sankerib sovereign of ah-shoor,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Therefore thus said (YAHUAH) HWHY concerning the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘He does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.
items.kk: Therefore thus said YAHUAH concerning the sovereign of ah-shoor, He does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: ‘By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And into this city he does not come,’ declares (YAHUAH) HWHY.
items.kk: By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And into this city he does not come, declares YAHUAH.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: ‘And I shall defend this city, to save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant Dawiḏ.’ ”
items.kk: And I shall defend this city, to save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant dah-veed.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a mal'ak of (YAHUAH) HWHY went out and killed in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they arose early in the morning and saw all of them, dead bodies.
items.kk: And a mahl-ahk of YAHUAH went out and killed in the camp of ah-shoor one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they arose early in the morning and saw all of them, dead bodies.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Sanḥĕriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur broke camp and went away and turned back and remained at Ninewĕh.
items.kk: And Sankerib the sovereign of ah-shoor broke camp and went away and turned back and remained at Nineweh.

items.name: narrator
items.text: “He does not come into this city.” You add it beneath the rest, with the date. The scroll is heavier than it was.
items.kk: He does not come into this city. You add it beneath the rest, with the date. The scroll is heavier than it was.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The road to Laḵish is quiet. The springs you stopped will be opened again.

items.name: narrator
items.text: In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick and near death. And Yahshayahu the naḇi, the son of Amots, came to him and said to him,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Thus said (YAHUAH) HWHY, ‘Set your house in order, for you are going to die and not live.’ ”
items.kk: Thus said YAHUAH, Set your house in order, for you are going to die and not live.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu turned his face toward the wall and prayed to (YAHUAH) HWHY,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu turned his face toward the wall and prayed to YAHUAH,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and said,
items.kk: and said,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “I pray, O (YAHUAH) HWHY, please remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a perfect heart and have done what is good in Your eyes.”
items.kk: I pray, O YAHUAH, please remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a perfect heart and have done what is good in Your eyes.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu wept bitterly.
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu wept bitterly.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the Word of (YAHUAH) HWHY came to Yahshayahu, saying,
items.kk: And the Word of YAHUAH came to yah-shah-yah-hoo, saying,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Go and say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said (YAHUAH) HWHY, the Aluahim of Dawiḏ your father, “I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. See, I am adding fifteen years to your days.
items.kk: Go and say to Kizqiyahu, Thus said YAHUAH, the al-oo-ah-heem of dah-veed your father, I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. See, I am adding fifteen years to your days.

items.name: divine
items.text: “And out of the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur I shall deliver you and this city and protect this city.”
items.kk: And out of the hand of the sovereign of ah-shoor I shall deliver you and this city and protect this city.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “And this is the sign to you from (YAHUAH) HWHY, that (YAHUAH) HWHY does this word which He has spoken:
items.kk: And this is the sign to you from YAHUAH, that YAHUAH does this word which He has spoken,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “See, I am bringing the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down with the sun on the sundial of Aḥaz, ten degrees backward.”
items.kk: See, I am bringing the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down with the sun on the sundial of ah-khahz, ten degrees backward.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the sun returned ten degrees on the dial by which it had gone down.
items.kk: And the sun returned ten degrees on the dial by which it had gone down.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The “sundial of Aḥaz” is in the Hebrew the “steps (ma‛aloth) of Aḥaz” — a stair by the house of the sovereign on which the shadow fell, step by step, as the sun went down.
items.kk: The sundial of ah-khahz is in the Hebrew the steps maaloth of ah-khahz, a stair by the house of the sovereign on which the shadow fell, step by step, as the sun went down.

items.name: narrator
items.text: For Yahshayahu had said,
items.kk: For yah-shah-yah-hoo had said,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Let them take a cake of figs and apply it on the boil, so that he lives.”
items.kk: Let them take a cake of figs and apply it on the boil, so that he lives.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu asked,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu asked,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “What is the sign that I go up to the House of (YAHUAH) HWHY?”
items.kk: What is the sign that I go up to the House of YAHUAH?

items.name: narrator
items.text: The shadow lies where it lay this morning. You count the steps twice.
items.kk: The shadow lies where it lay this morning. You count the steps twice.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Fifteen years, and a sign on the stair of Aḥaz. You write it under the word about the city.
items.kk: Fifteen years, and a sign on the stair of ah-khahz. You write it under the word about the city.

items.name: narrator
items.text: At that time Meroḏaḵ-Balaḏan son of Balaḏan, sovereign of Baḇal (Baḇylon), sent letters and a present to Ḥizqiyahu, for he heard that he had been sick and had recovered.
items.kk: At that time Merodak-Baladan son of Baladan, sovereign of bah-vahl babylon, sent letters and a present to Kizqiyahu, for he heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu was pleased with them and showed them the house of his treasures, the silver and gold, the spices and precious ointment and all his armoury and all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Ḥizqiyahu did not show them.
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu was pleased with them and showed them the house of his treasures, the silver and gold, the spices and precious ointment and all his armoury and all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Kizqiyahu did not show them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Yahshayahu the naḇi went to Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu and said to him,
items.kk: And yah-shah-yah-hoo the nah-vee went to Sovereign Kizqiyahu and said to him,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “What did these men say and from where did they come to you?”
items.kk: What did these men say and from where did they come to you?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu said,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu said,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “They came to me from a distant land, from Baḇal (Baḇylon).”
items.kk: They came to me from a distant land, from bah-vahl babylon.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “What have they seen in your house?”
items.kk: What have they seen in your house?

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “They have seen all that is in my house; there is not an object among my treasures that I did not show them.”
items.kk: They have seen all that is in my house, there is not an object among my treasures that I did not show them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: So Yahshayahu said to Ḥizqiyahu,
items.kk: So yah-shah-yah-hoo said to Kizqiyahu,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: “Hear the Word of (YAHUAH) HWHY of hosts:
items.kk: Hear the Word of YAHUAH of hosts,

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: ‘See, the days are coming when all that is in your house and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be taken away to Baḇal (Baḇylon); not a matter shall be left,’ declares (YAHUAH) HWHY.
items.kk: See, the days are coming when all that is in your house and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be taken away to bah-vahl babylon, not a matter shall be left, declares YAHUAH.

items.name: yahshayahu
items.text: ‘And they shall take some of your sons who are born to you, whom you bring forth. And they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the sovereign of Baḇal (Baḇylon).’ ”
items.kk: And they shall take some of your sons who are born to you, whom you bring forth. And they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the sovereign of bah-vahl babylon.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yahshayahu,
items.kk: And Kizqiyahu said to yah-shah-yah-hoo,

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “The Word of (YAHUAH) HWHY which you have spoken is good!”
items.kk: The Word of YAHUAH which you have spoken is good!

items.name: hizqiyahu
items.text: “Because there is shalom and truth in my days.”
items.kk: Because there is shah-lohm and truth in my days.

items.name: narrator
items.text: A little over a hundred years later it came to pass: Baḇal took Yahrushalayim, carried off the treasures of the house of the sovereign and of the House of (YAHUAH) HWHY, and took the sons of the house of Dawiḏ into exile (2 Melaḵim 24-25; Dani’al 1:3).
items.kk: A little over a hundred years later it came to pass, bah-vahl took yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, carried off the treasures of the house of the sovereign and of the House of YAHUAH, and took the sons of the house of dah-veed into exile 2 Melakim 24, 25, dah-nee-ahl 1,3.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Under the word about the city spared, the word about the city taken. Both from the same mouth, both true.
items.kk: Under the word about the city spared, the word about the city taken. Both from the same mouth, both true.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The Seven Hundred Years. Ashshur · Baḇal · Persia · Greece · Rome
items.kk: The Seven Hundred Years. ah-shoor bah-vahl Persia Greece Rome

items.name: narrator
items.text: While Yahshayahu spoke in Yahrushalayim, far to the west a village of huts stood on a hill above the river Tiber. By its own reckoning it was founded in 753 BCE. Its name was Rome. In seven hundred years it will rule the world — and Yahuḏah with it.
items.kk: While yah-shah-yah-hoo spoke in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, far to the west a village of huts stood on a hill above the river Tiber. By its own reckoning it was founded in 753 B.C.E. Its name was Rome. In seven hundred years it will rule the world, and yah-hoo-dah with it.

items.name: narrator
items.text: 612 BCE — Ashshur falls. The empire that menaced the days of Yahshayahu is itself destroyed: Ninewĕh burns.
items.kk: 612 B.C.E. ah-shoor falls. The empire that menaced the days of yah-shah-yah-hoo is itself destroyed, Nineweh burns.

items.name: narrator
items.text: 586 BCE — the Hĕḵal destroyed. Baḇal (Baḇylon) takes Yahrushalayim, burns the Hĕḵal, and carries Yahuḏah into exile.
items.kk: 586 B.C.E. the hay-kahl destroyed. bah-vahl babylon takes yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, burns the hay-kahl, and carries yah-hoo-dah into exile.

items.name: narrator
items.text: 539 BCE — Koresh of Persia. Koresh sovereign of Persia takes Baḇal and lets the exiles go home to build again.
items.kk: 539 B.C.E. koh-resh of Persia. koh-resh sovereign of Persia takes bah-vahl and lets the exiles go home to build again.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And in the first year of Koresh sovereign of Persia, that the Word of (YAHUAH) HWHY by the mouth of Yahrmeyah might be accomplished, (YAHUAH) HWHY stirred up the ruach of Koresh sovereign of Persia, to proclaim throughout all his reign and also in writing, saying,
items.kk: And in the first year of koh-resh sovereign of Persia, that the Word of YAHUAH by the mouth of Yahrmeyah might be accomplished, YAHUAH stirred up the roo-ahk of koh-resh sovereign of Persia, to proclaim throughout all his reign and also in writing, saying,

items.name: narrator
items.text: 536 BCE — the foundation laid. The exiles come home to a city broken down and burnt. They build the altar again on its place, and in the second year they lay the foundation of the House.
items.kk: 536 B.C.E. the foundation laid. The exiles come home to a city broken down and burnt. They build the altar again on its place, and in the second year they lay the foundation of the House.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the builders laid the foundation of the Hĕḵal of (YAHUAH) HWHY,they appointed the kohanim in their robes, with trumpets and the Lĕwites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise (YAHUAH) HWHY, after the order of Dawiḏ sovereign of Yasharal.
items.kk: And when the builders laid the foundation of the hay-kahl of YAHUAH,they appointed the koh-hah-neem in their robes, with trumpets and the lay-vites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise YAHUAH, after the order of dah-veed sovereign of yah-shar-al.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they responded by praising and giving thanks to (YAHUAH) HWHY,
items.kk: And they responded by praising and giving thanks to YAHUAH,

items.name: people
items.text: “For He is good, for His kindness towards Yasharal is forever.”
items.kk: For He is good, for His kindness towards yah-shar-al is forever.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised (YAHUAH) HWHY, because the foundation of the House of (YAHUAH) HWHY was laid.
items.kk: And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised YAHUAH, because the foundation of the House of YAHUAH was laid.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And many of the kohanim and Lĕwites and heads of the fathers’ houses, the old men who had seen the first House, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this House was laid before their eyes and many shouted aloud for joy,
items.kk: And many of the koh-hah-neem and lay-vites and heads of the fathers houses, the old men who had seen the first House, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this House was laid before their eyes and many shouted aloud for joy,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and the people could not distinguish the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people, for the people shouted with a loud shout and the sound was heard far away.
items.kk: and the people could not distinguish the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people, for the people shouted with a loud shout and the sound was heard far away.

items.name: narrator
items.text: 331 BCE — Greece. Alexander of Macedon overthrows Persia; after him come the Greek kingdoms, and the struggle of the Maqqabim.
items.kk: 331 B.C.E. Greece. Alexander of Macedon overthrows Persia, after him come the Greek kingdoms, and the struggle of the Maqqabim.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “And the male goat is the sovereign of Greece and the large horn between its eyes is the first sovereign.
items.kk: And the male goat is the sovereign of Greece and the large horn between its eyes is the first sovereign.

items.name: narrator
items.text: 63 BCE — Rome. Rome takes Yahrushalayim. The village of huts on the Tiber is now the empire that will rule Yahuḏah when the child of the promise is born, and its soldiers stand on her roads.
items.kk: 63 B.C.E. Rome. Rome takes yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem. The village of huts on the Tiber is now the empire that will rule yah-hoo-dah when the child of the promise is born, and its soldiers stand on her roads.

items.name: danial
items.text: “And in the days of these sovereigns the Al of the shamayim shall set up a reign which shall never be destroyed, nor the reign pass on to other people – it crushes and puts to an end all these reigns and it shall stand forever.
items.kk: And in the days of these sovereigns the Al of the shah-mah-yeem shall set up a reign which shall never be destroyed, nor the reign pass on to other people, it crushes and puts to an end all these reigns and it shall stand forever.

items.text: But when the completion of the time came, Aluahim sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under Torah,

items.text: What follows first you did not see with your own eyes. It is shown as the Besorah tells it — the accounts kept by those who were there (Luke 1:2).
items.kk: What follows first you did not see with your own eyes. It is shown as the beh-soh-rah tells it, the accounts kept by those who were there Luke 1,2.

items.name: narrator
items.text: There was in the days of Herodes, the sovereign of Yahuḏah, a certain kohen named Zaḵaryahu, of the division of Aḇiyah. And his wife was of the daughters of Aharon and her name was Alisheḇa.
items.kk: There was in the days of Herodes, the sovereign of yah-hoo-dah, a certain kohen named zah-khar-yah-hoo, of the division of Abiyah. And his wife was of the daughters of Aharon and her name was Alisheba.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were both righteous before Aluahim, blamelessly walking in all the commands and righteousnesses of (YAHUAH) HWHY.
items.kk: And they were both righteous before al-oo-ah-heem, blamelessly walking in all the commands and righteousnesses of YAHUAH.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they had no child, because Alisheḇa was barren and both were advanced in years.
items.kk: And they had no child, because Alisheba was barren and both were advanced in years.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it came to be, that while he was serving as kohen before Aluahim in the order of his division,
items.kk: And it came to be, that while he was serving as kohen before al-oo-ah-heem in the order of his division,

items.name: narrator
items.text: according to the institute of the kehunnah, he was chosen by lot to burn incense when he went into the Dwelling Place of (YAHUAH) HWHY.
items.kk: according to the institute of the kehunnah, he was chosen by lot to burn incense when he went into the Dwelling Place of YAHUAH.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the entire crowd of people was praying outside at the hour of incense.
items.kk: And the entire crowd of people was praying outside at the hour of incense.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Twice a day, morning and evening, a kohen chosen by lot went alone into the Set Apart Place and burned incense on the golden altar before the veil, while the people prayed outside. Many kohanim never had the lot fall to them in their whole lives.
items.kk: Twice a day, morning and evening, a kohen chosen by lot went alone into the Set Apart Place and burned incense on the golden altar before the veil, while the people prayed outside. Many koh-hah-neem never had the lot fall to them in their whole lives.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a mal'ak of (YAHUAH) HWHY appeared to him, standing on the right side of the mizbe'ach of incense.
items.kk: And a mahl-ahk of YAHUAH appeared to him, standing on the right side of the miz-beh-ahk of incense.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when Zaḵaryahu saw him, he was troubled and fear fell upon him.
items.kk: And when zah-khar-yah-hoo saw him, he was troubled and fear fell upon him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But the mal'ak said to him,
items.kk: But the mahl-ahk said to him,

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “Do not be afraid, Zaḵaryahu, for your prayer is heard. And your wife Alisheḇa shall bear you a son and you shall call his name Yahuchanon.
items.kk: Do not be afraid, zah-khar-yah-hoo, for your prayer is heard. And your wife Alisheba shall bear you a son and you shall call his name yah-hoo-kah-nohn.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “And you shall have joy and gladness and many shall rejoice at his birth.
items.kk: And you shall have joy and gladness and many shall rejoice at his birth.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “For he shall be great before (YAHUAH) HWHY and shall drink no wine and strong drink at all. And he shall be filled with the Ruach HaQadash, even from his mother’s womb.
items.kk: For he shall be great before YAHUAH and shall drink no wine and strong drink at all. And he shall be filled with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh, even from his mother's womb.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “And he shall turn many of the children of Yasharal to (YAHUAH) HWHY their Aluahim.
items.kk: And he shall turn many of the children of yah-shar-al to YAHUAH their al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “And he shall go before Him in the ruach and power of Aliyahu, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the insight of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for (YAHUAH) HWHY.”
items.kk: And he shall go before Him in the roo-ahk and power of ah-lee-yah-hoo, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the insight of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for YAHUAH.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Zaḵaryahu said to the mal'ak,
items.kk: And zah-khar-yah-hoo said to the mahl-ahk,

items.name: zakaryahu
items.text: “By what shall I know this? For I am old and my wife advanced in years.”
items.kk: By what shall I know this? For I am old and my wife advanced in years.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the mal'ak answering, said to him,
items.kk: And the mahl-ahk answering, said to him,

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “I am Gaḇri’al, who stands in the presence of Aluahim and was sent to speak to you and announce to you this besorah.
items.kk: I am gahv-ree-ahl, who stands in the presence of al-oo-ah-heem and was sent to speak to you and announce to you this beh-soh-rah.

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “But see, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day this takes place, because you did not believe my words which shall be filled in their appointed time. ”
items.kk: But see, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day this takes place, because you did not believe my words which shall be filled in their appointed time.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the people waited for Zaḵaryahu and marvelled at his delay in the Dwelling Place.
items.kk: And the people waited for zah-khar-yah-hoo and marvelled at his delay in the Dwelling Place.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when he came out, he was unable to speak to them. And they recognised that he had seen a vision in the Dwelling Place, for he was beckoning to them and remained dumb.
items.kk: And when he came out, he was unable to speak to them. And they recognised that he had seen a vision in the Dwelling Place, for he was beckoning to them and remained dumb.

items.text: “He has seen something in there,” your father says, “and it has taken his voice.”
items.kk: He has seen something in there, your father says, and it has taken his voice.

items.kk: And it came to be, as soon as the days of his service were completed, he went away to his house.

items.text: And in the sixth month the mal'ak Gaḇri’al was sent by Aluahim to a city of Galil named Natsareth,
items.kk: And in the sixth month the mahl-ahk gahv-ree-ahl was sent by al-oo-ah-heem to a city of gah-leel named nahts-ah-ret,

items.text: to a maiden engaged to a man whose name was Yosĕph, of the house of Dawiḏ. And the maiden’s name was Miryam.

items.text: And the mal'ak, coming to her, said,
items.kk: And the mahl-ahk, coming to her, said,

items.name: gabrial
items.text: “Greetings, favoured one, the Master is with you. Baruk are you among women!”
items.kk: Greetings, favoured one, the Master is with you. Baruk are you among women!

items.kk: But she was greatly disturbed at his word and wondered what kind of greeting this was.

items.kk: And the mahl-ahk said to her,

items.kk: Do not marvel that I said to you, You have to be born from above.

items.name: yahusha mashiach

items.kk: The roo-ahk breathes where it wishes, and you hear the sound of it, but do not know where it comes from and where it goes. So is everyone who has been born of the roo-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Naḵdimon answered and said to Him,
items.kk: Nakdimon answered and said to Him,

items.text: “How is it possible for this to take place?”
items.kk: How is it possible for this to take place?

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Are you the teacher of Yasharal, and do not know this?
items.kk: Are you the teacher of yah-shar-al, and do not know this?

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Truly, truly, I say to you, We speak what We know and witness what We have seen, and you do not receive Our witness.
items.kk: Truly, truly, I say to you, We speak what We know and witness what We have seen, and you do not receive Our witness.

items.kk: If you do not believe when I spoke to you about earthly matters, how are you going to believe when I speak to you about the heavenly matters?

items.text: “And no one has gone up into the shamayim except He who came down from the shamayim – the Son of Aḏam.

items.text: so that whoever is believing in Him should not perish but possess everlasting life.

items.text: “For Aluahim so loved the world that He gave His only brought-forth Son, so that everyone who believes in Him should not perish but possess everlasting life.

items.kk: He who believes in Him is not judged, but he who does not believe is judged already, because he has not believed in the Name of the only brought-forth Son of al-oo-ah-heem.

items.text: “And this is the mishpat, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were wicked.

items.kk: For everyone who is practising evil matters hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works should be exposed.

items.kk: Master, You have no vessel, and the well is deep. From where, then, do You have living water?

items.kk: but whoever drinks of the water I give him shall certainly never thirst. And the water that I give him shall become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.

items.kk: for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband. What you have said is true.
